sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly define light as a wave (amplitude and phase). Introduce 'interference'—the phenomenon where two waves superimpose to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or same amplitude.
sections.example: Visualize two ripples in a pond colliding; where peaks meet, the water rises higher (constructive interference).

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: Diffraction
sections.content: Explain diffraction: the bending of light waves around obstacles or through apertures. Introduce the 'Huygens-Fresnel Principle'—each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining through a tiny pinhole creates a distinct pattern of bright and dark rings on a wall, rather than just a dot.

sections.title: The Holographic Process (Recording)
sections.content: Explain how holography captures both amplitude and phase. A reference beam (direct light) and an object beam (reflected from object) meet on a film. The interference pattern is 'frozen' as a diffraction grating.
sections.example: An Iron Man helmet reflecting a laser beam onto a holographic film, creating a complex 'fingerprint' pattern that looks like static noise.

sections.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the Image
sections.content: Explain that when the original reference beam hits the 'static noise' (hologram), it diffracts to recreate the original wavefronts, tricking the eye into seeing a 3D object.
sections.example: Shining a flashlight through the Iron Man 'fingerprint' film, projecting a ghost-like, 3D floating image of the helmet in thin air.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Synthesize the logic: Diffraction records the data, and interference reconstructs the 3D reality. Mention applications in security (banknotes) and high-density data storage.
sections.example: The shimmering 'dove' logo on a credit card is a transmission hologram that changes depth as you tilt it.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
lecture_lines: Light propagates as a wave with amplitude and phase.
Waves superimpose, leading to constructive or destructive interference.
Visualize ripples colliding to form patterns.
animations: Fade in two sine waves moving horizontally. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight wave peak overlap as constructive interference. (Color: #FF0000)
Highlight wave peak-trough overlap as destructive interference. (Color: #0000FF)

storyboard.title: The Core Mechanism: Diffraction
lecture_lines: Diffraction is light bending around obstacles.
Huygens-Fresnel: each point acts as a source.
animations: Show a flat wavefront hitting a pinhole. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Animate secondary circular wavelets emanating from the pinhole. (Color: #00FF00)
Show the spherical wave pattern spreading out. (Color: #FFFFFF)

storyboard.title: The Holographic Process (Recording)
lecture_lines: Holography captures both light amplitude and phase.
Reference and object beams meet on film.
Interference patterns are frozen as a grating.
animations: Show two incoming beams hitting a screen. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Draw the resulting complex interference fringes. (Color: #FFFF00)
Fade in the 'frozen' grating structure representing the hologram. (Color: #FF00FF)
Highlight the recorded data as a static pattern. (Color: #AAAAAA)
Summarize the process as 'recording phase + amplitude'. (Color: #FFFFFF)

storyboard.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the Image
lecture_lines: Reference beam illuminates the recorded grating.
Light diffracts to reconstruct original wavefronts.
animations: Shine a reference beam through the hologram. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show light diffracting out from the grating. (Color: #00FFFF)
Fade in the visual ghost-image of the object. (Color: #FFCC00)
Label the reconstruction as '3D Wavefront Recovery'. (Color: #FFFFFF)

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Diffraction records data; interference reconstructs reality.
Used in security features like credit cards.
animations: Show the shimmering credit card hologram. (Color: #00FF00)
